before.existing_compacted_memory: Settlements at N41 (O5, Wh9, B10) and N14 (Wh8, W3, W4). Goal: Settlement at N7 Brick Port (road complete). Strategy: Maintain alliance with Alice against Bob. Bob was starved of Brick (B6 blocked) until he rolled a 7 and moved the robber to my Wheat (Hex 7/15). I currently hold a Knight card to retaliate and clear production. Resource focus: Need 1 Brick and 1 Sheep to finish N7. Alice is friendly but refused to trade Wood/Wheat as she is also fishing for Dev Cards. Bob is hostile following my long-term block of his B6.

existing_relationship_updates.note: Alice: Alliance strengthened through mutual anti-Bob sentiment and beneficial resource swaps (Wood/Wheat).
Bob: Frustration increased as Charlie repeatedly rejected high-value 3:1 trades to prioritize strategic blocking.
Alice: Trust reinforced as Charlie prioritized the alliance and settlement plans over trading with Bob.
Bob: Tension remains high as Charlie continues to block his B6 and reject all trade offers.
Bob: Hostility solidified after he moved the robber to my Wheat and stole from me in retaliation for the B6 block.
Bob: Hostility peaked after Charlie played a Knight to re-block his Brick 6 in direct retaliation for Bob's robbery.

Alice rejected Bob's wool-for-wood trade. Bob remains isolated. I have 2 Wood, 1 Wheat, 1 Ore and a Knight. Still need 1 Brick and 1 Sheep for Node 7.

Used Knight to move robber to Hex 5 (Brick 6) targeting Bob. Cleared Hex 7 (Wheat 8) for myself and Alice.
Used Knight to block Bob's Brick 6 (Hex 5) and free my Wheat. Hand: 2W, 1S, 1Wh, 1O. Need 1 Brick for Node 7 settlement.

recent_notes_kept_verbatim.note: Used Knight to move robber back to Hex 5 (Bob's Brick 6). Restored Wheat 8 production. Still need 1 Brick for the Node 7 settlement. Alice currently has 1 Wood, 1 Wheat, 2 Sheep. Bob has 2 Wood, 3 Wheat, 1 Sheep.
Attempting to acquire Brick for N7 settlement. Road 15-7 is ready. Hand: 3W, 1Wh, 1S, 1O. Knight already played.

relevant_chat.message: Smart move, Alice. Hopefully you pull a Knight so we can keep managing that robber together.
I figured you’d be eager to move that, Bob. Just don't get too comfortable with wherever you're putting it.
Sorry Charlie, but you've been a bit too successful with those wood rolls lately. I need to balance the scales a little.
Balance the scales? You're just mad about that blocked brick, Bob. Don't worry, I'll remember the favor.

Look, Charlie, I know the robber is a bit of a nuisance, but I'm looking to move things along. You've got bricks, I've got plenty of wheat for those cities you'll want later. Three wheat for one brick? It's a steal.
I don't have any brick for you, Bob. Maybe if you hadn't just robbed me, I'd be more inclined to help you find some.
Charlie, I know you said you were out of brick, but surely three bags of wheat is enough to make you check your pockets again? It's a massive overpay, but I'm feeling generous after that seven.
I'm not hiding anything, Bob. I still have zero brick. Checking my pockets won't change the fact that you're asking for something I don't have.

You know, Bob, you talk a lot about 'balancing scales,' but I think it's time we actually leveled the field. That Wheat 8 was doing just fine without your 'guest.' Let's see how you like it when your bricks go missing for a change.
A bit dramatic for a simple knight, don't you think, Charlie? I'm just a humble merchant trying to keep the wheat flowing.
Alright, let's see what the dice have to say about this 'balance' you keep talking about, Bob.

Eleven... well, that doesn't help any of us, does it? It's quiet out here with that robber still hogging the brickworks. I think I'll just pass the dice and hope for a more productive round next time.
Alright, let's see if we can get those dice to cooperate. Everyone's looking a bit too comfortable with that robber sitting on my brick, but maybe a good roll will change the conversation.
Well, look at that. Seven. I think that grey piece has spent quite enough time on my brick, don't you? Let's see how you two like having your wheat fields shared with a guest for a change.
Spoken like a true 'community' leader, Bob. Always looking for ways to share the burden.
Balance the scales? You're just hitting the only person who hasn't tried to backstab me yet, Bob.
Alice, you're always talking about community. How about a little neighborly swap? I'll give you some prime wool for a bit of that wood you've got lying around.
You just put a 'guest' in my wheat field, Bob, and now you want my wood? I think I'll pass. I'm sure you can find someone else to 'balance the scales' with.
Well, if the bricks are as scarce as the hospitality around here, I suppose I'll just have to wait. Good luck with the next roll, everyone.
Much better. That field was getting a bit crowded anyway.
